::: {.lede}
I teach across three areas at SUNY Brockport, at both the undergraduate and
graduate levels.
:::

**Course materials, assignments, and grades live in the learning management
system.** This page is the public description of what each course covers — if you
are enrolled, everything you need is in the LMS.

## Operations Research & Management

::: {.course}
[CIS 427/527 · Undergraduate & Graduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Information Systems Project Management and Practice**

Managing information-systems projects across the Systems Development Life Cycle:
planning, scheduling, risk, UML Modeling, and team delivery, using
industry-standard tools.
:::

::: {.course}
[BIT 2406 · Undergraduate]{.course-code} [Virginia Tech]{.tag}<br>
**Business Statistics, Analytics & Modeling**

Optimization and decision modeling for business — Linear and Network Programming,
Multicriteria Decision Making, Decision Analysis, and Forecasting.
:::

## Information Systems & Business Analytics

::: {.course}
[CIS 102 · Undergraduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Fundamentals of Information Systems**

How Information Systems create value in organizations — system types, IT
infrastructure, Data Management, and the ethics of use.
:::

::: {.course}
[CIS 422 · Undergraduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Database Management Systems**

Database design and implementation end to end: ER Modeling, Normalization, SQL,
and a semester-long team database application.
:::

## Programming & Computation

::: {.course}
[CSC 120 · Undergraduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Introduction to Computing**

A first programming course, in Java — variables, control flow, methods, and
arrays, with hands-on labs.
:::

::: {.course}
[CIS 117 · Undergraduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Introduction to Web Development**

Foundations of web development — HTML5, CSS, and page structure — building up to a
personal website.
:::

::: {.course}
[CSC 602 · Graduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Deep Learning**

Neural networks and modern Deep Learning methods, from foundations to applied
implementation.
:::

## First-year & advising

::: {.course}
[GEP 100 · Undergraduate]{.course-code}<br>
**Academic Planning Seminar (First-Year Experience)**

A first-year seminar on academic success, study strategies, planning, and campus
resources.
:::

Beyond coursework, I advise undergraduate and graduate students and mentor
student research — see [Ongoing projects](ongoing-projects.qmd) and the students
note on the [Research](research.qmd) page.

## Office hours

Listed in the LMS each semester. Email me if none of the posted times work.
